newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam urges patriotic zeal amid reform woes.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam urges patriotic zeal amid reform woes.

text.p: Vietnam, facing its most uncertain period since launching reforms in the late 1980s, marked the 52nd anniversary of its 1945 communist uprising on Tuesday by calling for a renewed spirit of revolutionary zeal.

Red-ink banners splashed across the front pages of official newspapers declared that the spirit of the August 1945 revolution should be revived in order to propel the Doi Moi (renovation) process through its current difficulties.

"Regaining power from the colonial rulers was a very difficult task, but building and improving the socialist state and its governing body is even more difficult," the Communist Party's Nhan Dan newspaper said, beneath a photo of the late president Ho Chi Minh.
It added that communist party members and other citizens should "display their zeal" to see the country emerge on par with economic powers elsewhere in the world.

Vietnam's decade-old experiment with free-market reforms has been hit this year by a series of economic problems and concerns over social issues including recent unrest in northern areas of the country.
Foreign investment sentiment has dipped sharply -- some estimates say by up to 60 percent -- causing Vietnam to lose its earlier lustre as one of East Asia's brightest new emerging economic stars.
Two major conglomerates have been rocked by fraud and corruption scandals with far-reaching implications for the nascent banking industry.

Meanwhile, the political climate has been dogged by growing questioning of the management of the reform process, and uncertainty amid a prolonged search for a new generation of leaders to replace the ageing triumvirate of President Le Duc Anh, Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet and Communist party chief Do Muoi.

The August 19 anniversary is a major event on Vietnam's political calendar, commemorating the date in 1945 when Ho Chi Minh seized the opportunity during a power vacuum at the end of World War Two to declare Vietnam's independence from colonial rule.
